The areas affected include, but are not limited to the following areas within the New Hope service delivery area: • Vista Drive • Westwood Drive and branch roads • Old Tails Creek Road west of Westwood Drive • Roberts Ridge Road and all branch roads • Craigtown Road and all branch roads • Hwy 52 West, west of Hancock Drive and all branch roads • New Hope Road and all branch roads • Tower Road and all branch roads • Village Park Drive • Highway 282 from Courier Street west to Pleasant Grove Church • Evans Road • Mountainview Drive • Summit Drive and all branch roads In order to protect the public from a potential health hazard, customers that have experienced water outages and/or low pressures are advised to use only boiled tap water or bottled water for drinking, cooking, or preparing food. To properly boil tap water for use, customers should: • Heat water until bubbles come quickly from the bottom of the container; • Continue heating the water for one minute once it begins to boil; • Remove the water from the heat source and allow to cool before use. During a Boil Water Advisory, the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) recommends that boiled tap water or bottled water be used for the following activities: • Drinking • Brushing Teeth • Washing food and preparing food and baby formula • Making ice • Drinking water for pets Other activities such as clothes washing, dishwashing, and other uses can be performed without boiling tap water, if performed properly. Nazlini Wash, Black Rock Canyon, Coyote Wash, Muerto, Canyon del, Sheep Dip Creek, Agua Sal Creek, Chinle Wash and Tiis Ndiitsooi Wash. Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become flooded as well. West Central Piute County in central Utah... East Central Beaver County in southern Utah... * Until 1000 PM MDT. * At 659 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the Cottonwood Burn Scar in Beaver County. Between 0.25 and 0.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow moving through the Beaver River into the Grove area within Beaver. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials. The debris flow has not yet reached the upper camera in Beaver Canyon. Once the debris flow reaches the upper camera at the diversion dam, expect the flow to reach the Grove area 1 to 1.5 hours later. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing flash flooding. SOURCE...Radar. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Beaver. This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches in the Cottonwood Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety. Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.
